conventions.convention: Midpoint uses strictly increasing endpoints, integer n ≥ 1, h=(b-a)/n, and indices 0 ≤ j < n. Invalid endpoints or panel counts return invalid-grid.
Simpson n counts subintervals, must be even and at least two, and produces n/2 two-subinterval blocks. A block of total length L has coefficient L/6.
The quadrature procedures use exact-real arithmetic; their derivative-norm error bounds exclude evaluation and summation roundoff.
Both panel error identities use integral minus quadrature. The midpoint kernel is nonnegative; the Simpson kernel is nonpositive.
C^k on a closed interval requires continuous derivatives through order k, with endpoint derivatives interpreted one-sidedly.
Convex bracketing explicitly assumes Darboux integrability and requires no differentiability.

load_bearing.statement: For a<b, L=b-a, m=(a+b)/2 and f∈C^4([a,b]), S=L(f(a)+4f(m)+f(b))/6 satisfies ∫f−S=∫K f⁽⁴⁾. Here K(x)=(x-a)^3(3(x-a)-2L)/72 on [a,m] and K(x)=(b-x)^3(3(b-x)-2L)/72 on [m,b]; K≤0 and ∫|K|=L^5/2880.
Let a<b, let n≥2 be an even integer, and put h=(b-a)/n. If f∈C^4([a,b]), set M₄=max|f⁽⁴⁾| on [a,b]. Then |∫f−Q_S(f;a,b,n)|≤(b-a)h^4 M₄/180.

For a<b, an even integer n≥2, and an everywhere-evaluable real-valued f on [a,b], put h=(b-a)/n and x_j=a+jh; return Q_S=(h/3)Σ_{j<n/2}(f(x_{2j})+4f(x_{2j+1})+f(x_{2j+2})). Invalid endpoints or n<2 return invalid-grid; remaining odd n returns invalid-Simpson-panel-count.

For a<b, m=(a+b)/2 and f∈C^2([a,b]), K(t)=(t-a)^2/2 on [a,m] and K(t)=(b-t)^2/2 on [m,b] is continuous and nonnegative. Then ∫f−(b-a)f(m)=∫Kf'', with absolute error at most (b-a)^3 max|f''|/24; if f''≥0, the midpoint value does not exceed the integral.
Let a<b, let n≥1 be an integer, and put h=(b-a)/n. If f∈C^2([a,b]), define M₂=max|f''| on [a,b]. Then |∫f−Q_M(f;a,b,n)|≤(b-a)h²M₂/24.

For a<b, an integer n≥1, and an everywhere-evaluable real-valued f on [a,b], put h=(b-a)/n and m_j=a+(j+1/2)h for 0≤j<n; return Q_M=hΣ_{j<n}f(m_j). If a≥b or n<1, return invalid-grid without evaluating f.
Let a<b, let n≥2 be an even integer, and let p(x)=c₀+c₁x+c₂x²+c₃x³ with real coefficients. Then ∫_a^b p(x) dx=Q_S(p;a,b,n).

alerts.finding: Fact F1 says the Simpson kernel has "the two cubic pieces displayed in its Statement" in lem-simpson-panel-peano-kernel. The cited pieces are (x-a)^3(3(x-a)-2L)/72 and its reflection, hence quartic polynomials with nonzero leading coefficient 1/24. The sign, mass and error identity are otherwise quoted correctly.

The Definition assumes only "let f be real-valued at the nodes of the uniform grids with n and 2n subintervals" and then defines both values "using [[alg-composite-simpson-rule]]". That supplier requires a real-valued function on all of [a,b] evaluable at every point. The sampled-data premise does not supply that input contract. The finite formulas are meaningful, but a total extension or an explicit formula-only interpretation is left unstated.

The Definition begins "Let Q:[0,1]→R be a finite quadrature functional" and immediately writes Q(g)=Σ w_i g(x_i). A map with domain [0,1] takes scalar arguments, whereas this expression takes a function g as its argument. The declared domain is mistyped; the intended finite functional on functions is clear from the formula.

seams_checked.note: Contextual page prerequisite only. The assigned proofs use local integration-by-parts kernels, not an interpolation remainder or interpolation uniqueness theorem.

Page prose explicitly limits the supplier to smooth-integrand midpoint and Simpson rules. It does not claim a fractional-kernel theorem; local power-kernel integration and generating-function arguments supply those results.

Midpoint calls use n=1 separately on positive-width cells, or positive integer subpanel counts. The smooth convergence proof applies the C² estimate to smooth fertility and reaction integrands with the correct 1/24 constant.

Contextual prerequisite with no direct batch-20 item citation. The fixed-pivot quadrature estimate is derived locally from barycentric displacement and Lipschitz bounds; it does not import a C² midpoint bound for merely Lipschitz kernels.
Contextual prerequisite. Romberg directly uses the canonical published trapezoid definition; the page does not attribute its Euler–Maclaurin expansion or general Peano theorem to batch 20.

Two limited mismatches are recorded in alerts: the asymptotic lemma calls quartic kernel pieces cubic, and the indicator definition supplies only nodal data to a supplier requiring an everywhere-evaluable function. The kernel sign and mass, C⁴ restriction, even panel counts, and certified one-block constant L^5/2880 are otherwise faithful.

Levels use even panel counts 2^(ℓ+1)≥2. Simpson weights, degree-three exactness and the unit-interval bound 1/(180N^4) are quoted correctly. The hierarchy's separate functional-domain typo is recorded in alerts.

The tensor evaluator supplies everywhere-evaluable interpolants and valid even grids. Its error proof applies the scalar C⁴ estimate componentwise and retains the interval-length factors and separate vector norm factor.

The P1 stiffness argument applies midpoint with n=1 independently on each positive-width cell. The integrand is C² there; the h_K^3/24 bound is correct. Continuity and positive interval measure justify replacing the ordinary maximum by the essential supremum.
Mass assembly uses [0,π] with even M≥2. The proof establishes C⁴ regularity of the transformed trigonometric integrand before using πh^4 max|g⁽⁴⁾|/180, including the zero-degree case.
